modelFaq.title: How Ouiboo works
modelFaq.intro: Ouiboo is the technology that connects you with travel agencies. Ouiboo does not sell trips, and you always pay the agency directly — Ouiboo never holds your money.

whoSells.question: Who sells my trip?
whoSells.answer: The agency sells and organises your trip. Ouiboo provides the technology for finding, booking and managing it.

payDirect.question: Who do I pay?
payDirect.answer: You pay the agency directly — never Ouiboo. Ouiboo never holds your money.

stagedPayments.question: How do payments work?
stagedPayments.answer: For group trips, you pay a deposit of at most 30% directly to the agency. The balance is only requested after the group minimum is confirmed. If the minimum is not reached, the agency refunds your deposit.

refunds.question: Who refunds me?
refunds.answer: The agency that sold you the trip is responsible for refunds — it is the refund obligor. Ouiboo helps you follow the case and monitors the deadlines, but the refund itself is paid by the agency.

verification.question: How are agencies checked?
verification.answer: Before an agency can publish trips, its travel licence and insurance are checked. Each agency and trip page shows the licence status, its expiry date and the date it was verified, and the date its insurance was verified.

section1.title: Information we process
section1.body: Ouiboo processes information you provide when joining the waitlist, creating an account, managing an agency, publishing a trip, making a booking, contacting support, or completing a payment workflow. This can include identity and contact details, agency information, booking records, and transaction references.

section2.title: Why we use it
section2.body: We use this information to provide and secure the marketplace, fulfill bookings, communicate service updates, prevent abuse, meet legal obligations, and improve the product. We do not sell personal information.

section3.title: Optional analytics
section3.body: No analytics tracker runs by default on Ouiboo. Always-on analytics have been removed; optional analytics are never loaded unless you explicitly choose to allow them, and you can change that choice at any time. Language and security-related storage may still be used because it is necessary to provide the site.

section4.title: Sharing and retention
section4.body: Information is shared only with service providers and marketplace participants when needed to operate the requested service, or when required by law. Records are retained only as long as needed for service, security, accounting, dispute resolution, and legal purposes.

section5.title: Your choices
section5.body: Depending on applicable law, you may ask to access, correct, delete, restrict, or export your personal information, or object to certain processing. Use the contact channel shown in your Ouiboo account or service emails to submit a privacy request.

tangier.name: Tangier
tangier.title: Tangier travel guide
tangier.description: What to see and do in Tangier, Morocco — the medina, the Kasbah, Cap Spartel and the meeting of two seas. Bookings are not open yet; join the waitlist.
tangier.intro: Tangier sits where the Mediterranean meets the Atlantic: a port city of whitewashed medina lanes, café terraces and sea views in every direction. This guide covers the places travellers ask about most, in roughly the order you might walk them.

highlights.title: The Kasbah and the medina
highlights.text: Start at the Kasbah quarter for the views over the strait, then walk down through the medina lanes toward the Grand Socco — the square that joins the old town to the new.

highlights.title: Cap Spartel and the Caves of Hercules
highlights.text: West of the city, the lighthouse at Cap Spartel marks the meeting of the two seas; the Caves of Hercules sit just below it on the Atlantic side.

highlights.title: Cafés and the corniche
highlights.text: Tangier café culture is part of the visit: mint tea on a terrace, then a walk along the corniche as the light changes over the bay.

worldCup.title: Tangier and the 2030 World Cup
worldCup.text: Tangier is one of the Moroccan host cities for the 2030 FIFA World Cup, with matches planned at the Grand Stade de Tanger (Ibn Batouta Stadium). This page will grow as the tournament approaches — what to see between matches and how the city prepares. Join the waitlist for updates.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Tangier?
faq.a: Spring and autumn bring mild weather for walking the medina and the coast. Summer is warm and busy; winter is quieter and can be windy on the strait.

faq.q: How do I get to Tangier?
faq.a: Tangier has an international airport (Ibn Battouta), a ferry port with links to Spain, and Al Boraq high-speed trains to Rabat and Casablanca from Tanger Ville station.

faq.q: Can I book trips in Tangier on OuiBoo yet?
faq.a: Not yet. Bookings are not open while OuiBoo runs its closed beta. Join the waitlist and we will email you when bookings open.

tetouan.name: Tétouan
tetouan.title: Tétouan travel guide
tetouan.description: What to see and do in Tétouan, Morocco — the UNESCO-listed medina, the Ensanche and a centre for traditional crafts. Bookings are not open yet; join the waitlist.
tetouan.intro: Tétouan, between the Rif mountains and the Mediterranean, is known for its Andalusian heritage — its medina is a UNESCO World Heritage site — and for a slower pace than its larger neighbour, Tangier.

highlights.title: The medina (UNESCO)
highlights.text: One of Morocco’s most complete medinas, shaped by Andalusian refugees from Spain: white lanes, small squares and artisan workshops — still a working town rather than a museum.

highlights.title: The Ensanche and Feddan square
highlights.text: The Spanish-era new town next door: regular boulevards, the royal palace square (Feddan) and café terraces facing the mountains.

highlights.title: Artisans and markets
highlights.text: Tétouan is a centre for traditional crafts — weaving, pottery and painting — with workshops concentrated around the medina gates.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Tétouan?
faq.a: Spring and early autumn suit the medina lanes best. The nearby coast (Martil, M’diq) is busiest in summer.

faq.q: How do I get to Tétouan?
faq.a: Tétouan is about an hour by road from Tangier. Buses and shared taxis link it with Tangier and Chefchaouen; the nearest airports are in Tangier and Tétouan itself.

faq.q: Can I book trips in Tétouan on OuiBoo yet?
faq.a: Not yet. Bookings are not open while OuiBoo runs its closed beta. Join the waitlist and we will email you when bookings open.

chefchaouen.name: Chefchaouen
chefchaouen.title: Chefchaouen travel guide
chefchaouen.description: What to see and do in Chefchaouen, Morocco — the blue medina, Ras El Maa and the Rif mountains. Bookings are not open yet; join the waitlist.
chefchaouen.intro: Chefchaouen, in the Rif mountains, is the blue-washed mountain town travellers photograph from its kasbah and lanes — and also a working town of weavers, markets and trailheads into the Rif.

highlights.title: The blue medina
highlights.text: The old town’s blue-washed lanes climb from Place Uta el-Hammam, the main square, with the kasbah and the Grand Mosque.

highlights.title: Ras El Maa and the Spanish Mosque
highlights.text: Walk up to Ras El Maa, where the town’s water arrives, and continue to the Spanish Mosque on the hill for the classic view back over the blue town at sunset.

highlights.title: Into the Rif
highlights.text: Chefchaouen is the usual base for Rif mountain walks; the waterfalls and pools of Akchour are the best-known day out, reached by shared taxi.

faq.a: By most accounts the blue wash began in the town’s Jewish quarter in the 1930s, and residents kept repainting the lanes blue; the town itself now maintains the tradition.

faq.q: How do I get to Chefchaouen?
faq.a: Chefchaouen has no train station or airport: most travellers arrive by bus or shared taxi from Tangier or Tétouan — roughly two hours from Tangier.

faq.q: Can I book trips in Chefchaouen on OuiBoo yet?
faq.a: Not yet. Bookings are not open while OuiBoo runs its closed beta. Join the waitlist and we will email you when bookings open.

verification.title: How agency verification works
verification.description: The checks an agency passes before it can publish trips on OuiBoo: travel licence, civil-liability insurance and seller identity — and what verification does not claim.
verification.intro: OuiBoo is a technology platform: agencies sell their own trips, and travellers pay the agency directly. Before an agency can publish trips on OuiBoo, it passes a verification gate. This page explains what is checked — and what verification does not claim.

steps.title: Travel licence
steps.text: The agency submits its Law 11-16 travel licence (organiser-distributor — ODV — for agencies that organise trips). The licence number, issue date and issuing authority are recorded, and the licence document is checked against the issuing authority’s list where one is available.

steps.title: Civil-liability insurance
steps.text: The agency’s RC (responsabilité civile) insurance certificate is recorded — insurer, policy number and validity dates — and must be in force for trips to publish.

steps.title: Seller identity
steps.text: The agency’s legal name, registration and address are recorded, so the seller of record shown to travellers is the real business behind the listing.

steps.title: Expiry is enforced
steps.text: When a licence or insurance policy expires or fails verification, the agency’s listings pause automatically — there is no grace period.

verification.datedLine: This page describes the verification gate as it runs on 30 October 2026. Verification states what was checked and when; it is not a guarantee of any trip’s outcome.

faq.q: Does verification mean OuiBoo guarantees my trip?
faq.a: No. OuiBoo provides the technology; the agency is the seller of the trip and is responsible for delivering it. Verification covers the licence, insurance and identity records described on this page.

faq.q: Can I book a trip now?
faq.a: Not yet — bookings are not open during the closed beta. Join the waitlist to be told when they open.

faq.title: Straight answers
faq.intro: Who you pay, who refunds you, and what Ouiboo is — in plain words.

whoPay.q: Who do I pay for a trip?
whoPay.rest: — a deposit first (up to 30%), and the balance only once the trip's group minimum is confirmed. Ouiboo never holds traveller money, on any trip, ever.

whoRefund.q: Who refunds me if plans change?

charges.rest: Later fees will be published before they ever apply — charged to agencies as a monthly invoice, never added on top of the price you pay.

steps.title: How it starts
steps.intro: Three simple steps — with a human at the other end from the very first one.

step1.title: A 15-minute conversation
step1.text: We talk about your trips and your questions, on WhatsApp or by phone. No form before that conversation.

step2.title: You send three documents
step2.text: Your travel agency licence (ODV), your professional liability (RC) insurance and your trade-register registration. A WhatsApp photo is enough for each — and when the check is done, a dated record confirms it.

step3.title: Your first trips, published together
step3.text: We prepare your first trips with you — photos, itinerary, prices — and you approve every word before publication. Nothing appears without your agreement.

money.title: You are paid directly — always

direct.title: The traveller pays your agency
direct.text: A deposit (up to 30%) at booking, then the balance when the group minimum is confirmed. If the minimum is not reached, the deposit is refunded to the traveller in full.

never.title: Ouiboo never touches travellers' money
never.text: No payment ever passes through Ouiboo — not today, not later.

beta.title: During the beta: 0 MAD
beta.text: No subscription, no fees, nothing withheld from your payments.

money.guaranteeTitle: After the beta, our written commitment
money.guarantee: Any future fee will apply only through a published monthly invoice addressed to your agency, agreed in writing in advance, with notice and the right to leave before the first fee — and never deducted from traveller payments.

proof.title: What your travellers will see
proof.intro: Two examples — exactly what Ouiboo shows for an agency whose documents have been checked.
proof.recordNote: The same dated record is public on the agency's page and on every trip.
proof.passText: After a booking, the traveller receives a pass with a QR code: you scan it on the day of departure and attendance is confirmed.
proof.storefrontText: Your name, your trips and your dated verification record — a public page that proves who you are.

exclusive.q: Am I tied to Ouiboo exclusively?
exclusive.a: No. Publish on Ouiboo and everywhere else — your other channels are your business.

leave.q: Can I leave whenever I want?
leave.a: Yes, at any time and free of charge. Your trips, photos and reviews stay yours.

client.q: Does the client stay my client?
client.a: Yes. Your contact details appear on every booking, travellers contact you directly, and your name is on every trip and every review.

cancel.a: You do. Your cancellation scale is shown to the traveller before payment. If a dispute arises, a visible procedure applies — and you remain the organiser of the trip.

provide.q: What do I need to provide?
provide.a: Three documents: your licence, your RC insurance and your registration. A WhatsApp photo of each is enough to start.

golive.q: How long before I am live?
golive.a: Your documents are checked before anything goes live — that is the rule, for every agency. Then we prepare your first trips together and you approve them before publication.

french.a: Yes. French is enough to publish your trips; Arabic and English are a plus, never a condition.

computer.a: No. WhatsApp and a phone are enough to start — and for almost everything else.

honesty.title: What the beta is — and what it is not yet
items: Today, Ouiboo is a showcase: no booking and no payment is accepted yet.
Bookings will open with the founding agencies — not before.

During the beta, support is handled by the founder himself.
Founding agencies get a say in the product.
honesty.legal: Why this caution? Ouiboo is completing its legal formalities — activity classification and data protection — before opening bookings. So the beta starts as a showcase, openly.
